note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict: The item is not acceptable as it stands: one high and two medium findings survive. Most compliance checks pass. My gate re-run matches the author's report exactly: solvability 10/10 with 8 parallel workers, 485 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V6, 14 valid mutants, kill rate 1.0. The re-run rewrote items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-06/gates.json with identical content. Running build.py twice in a scratch mirror gave byte-identical task.json, reference.grc and variants, matching the committed files. The required fields are all present and correct: id/dir/split, tier, version, canary, licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbed=false and disjointness. The canary appears only in task.json (build.py imports the constant). The instruction does not mention benchmarks, oracles or canaries. Disjointness from reports/reference/training_task_specs.json holds. Tolerances follow the spec: ±1 % frequency, ±5 % amplitude, and band_fraction min 1/(1+1e-4), which is exactly 40 dB. The oracle is fair to correct alternatives. Hann, Blackman-Harris, Kaiser 40/45/50 dB, the Low-Pass Filter Taps variable, fcf with sine phase, Rational Resampler, PFB Decimator, no throttle and absolute sink paths all pass. Rectangular, Bartlett and Hilbert analytic-signal designs fail on numbers the instruction states. However: (1) the oracle accepts a graph with no down-converter at all; (2) the split depends on a Throttle that does nothing to the output, without which the chain hashes to train; (3) the instruction does not say how long the graph must run, yet V5 requires at least 4400 items per channel. Scratch evidence is in /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-06/ in WSL (shortcut.grc, probe.py, cand_*.grc, out_a/, out_b/).

findings.claim: V6 accepts a flowgraph that contains no input, no frequency shift, no filter and no decimation. The 'Expected result' paragraph fully describes both outputs, and the six checks look only at those outputs, so writing the described tones straight to the two File Sinks passes. P1 (real 40 kHz two-cosine input) and P2/P3 (the down-conversion itself) are therefore not actually verified. P1 is mapped to the rms checks, which this shows to be an overclaim.
findings.evidence: Scratch file /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-06/shortcut.grc has samp_rate 5000, a complex analog_sig_source_x at 400 Hz with amp 0.4 into a File Sink channel1.dat, and a complex one at -300 Hz with amp 0.25 into channel2.dat (4 functional blocks). Command: ./gb ladder shortcut.grc --task items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-06/task.json gives highest_passed=V6, first_failed=None. Check values: ch1 peak_freq 400.0, rms 0.399999, band_fraction 1.0; ch2 peak_freq -300.0, rms 0.249999, band_fraction 1.0. The 14 mutants all stay close to the reference, so the mutation gate never tests this kind of non-solution.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the outputs depend on processing a model cannot shortcut. Options: (a) add a seeded component to the input whose filtered and decimated version cannot be predicted from the instruction, e.g. low-level Gaussian noise from analog_noise_source_x with a stated seed, type and amplitude, or a seeded random-data modulated carrier. Then add corr_ref checks of each channel against the reference's captured output, with a spec-derived threshold. (b) At minimum, add an observation point on the generated input (e.g. a float File Sink input.dat named in the instruction) with peak/rms/band checks, so P1 is checked. Also consider dropping or softening the exact-output sentence in 'Expected result'. Re-run the gates and add the shortcut as a mutant or negative test.

findings.claim: The item lands in dev only because of a Throttle that the instruction does not ask for and that has no effect on the output. Without it, the reference chain's signature hashes to train. Training-side generators may therefore legitimately produce the same processing chain (sources -> add -> Frequency Xlating FIR -> File Sink). That defeats the purpose of the signature partition: a held-out chain should never be a template twin of a training chain.
findings.evidence: build.py docstring: 'The Throttle is part of the reference only ... it puts the chain signature in the dev partition (compose.signature_split). The instruction does not ask for it.' compose.signature_split computed in WSL: with the throttle, ('analog_sig_source_x','blocks_add_xx','blocks_throttle2','freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx','blocks_file_sink') -> dev. Without it, 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx|blocks_file_sink' -> train. The natural Float To Complex + xlating chain also hashes to train. compose.py says 'Training-side generators must check signature_split(sig) == "train"', so the throttle-free twin is allowed on the training side. Same pattern elsewhere in the set: gbf-dev-03 is dev with its throttle and train without it.
findings.suggested_fix: Test split discipline on a signature with inert blocks removed (throttle at least), either per item or in compose.signature for the whole set. If the stripped signature is train, change the processing chain itself. For example, 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|blocks_float_to_complex|freq_xlating_fft_filter_ccc|blocks_file_sink' hashes to dev without a throttle. Alternatively, record the stripped signature as reserved/non-train in splits/ so training generators cannot use it. Flag gbf-dev-03 for the same review.

findings.claim: V5 needs at least 4400 items at each channel output (about 35,200 input samples, 0.88 s at 40 kHz), but the instruction says nothing about run length. An answer that meets every stated requirement but caps the file-writing graph with a Head block of under about 35,200 input samples fails V5 liveness. Sibling build items avoid this with an explicit 'keep running' sentence, which this item lacks.
findings.evidence: Probe candidates (reference plus a float Head between combine and thr): head_20000 -> first_failed V5, 'liveness: an observation point received too few items {ch1: 2500, ch2: 2500}'. head_35000 -> first_failed V5, {ch1: 4375, ch2: 4375}. head_40000 -> passes V6. task.json observation.run has min_items 4400, which is stated only in the hidden contract. gbf-dev-01 and gbf-dev-02 say 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' gbf-dev-03, gbf-test-04 and gbf-test-07 have similar sentences. The gbf-dev-06 instruction has nothing comparable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the set-standard sentence to the instruction: 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' Rebuild with build.py and re-run the gates.

findings.claim: Two stated requirements cannot be checked by the oracle, and spec_properties do not say so. First, the filter cutoff of 1 kHz and transition width of 500 Hz: designs with clearly different values pass, and spec_properties do not list the filter parameters at all. Second, the 'real (float)' input in P1: a complex input with halved amplitudes passes, yet P1 claims to be checked via rms.
findings.evidence: Probe results: wrongspec_600_200, i.e. chan_taps = firdes.low_pass(1.0, samp_rate, 600, 200), passes V6 (ch2 band_fraction 1.0). wrongspec_1600_300 passes V6 (ch2 band_fraction 0.999997). complex_input_halfamp, with complex sources at amplitudes 0.4/0.25 and ccc xlating filters, passes V6 with rms 0.39981/0.249343. spec_properties P1-P5 contain no cutoff/transition property. The oracle maps P1 to the rms checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Either present the filter numbers as guidance (e.g. 'for example a low-pass filter with cutoff 1 kHz ...') and keep the 40 dB selectivity as the binding requirement, or list them in spec_properties marked as not behaviourally checkable with this input. Narrow P1's checked claim to what is observable, or add the input observation point from F1(b), which also makes the input's realness, rate and tones checkable.

findings.claim: The samp_rate -> 48000 mutation is labelled as breaking P2, but what it breaks is P1: the input is no longer at 40 kHz, and everything downstream scales consistently. The mutant is still valid and killed; only its 'breaks' label is wrong.
findings.evidence: task.json mutations[4]: {op: set_param, block: samp_rate, value: 48000, breaks: 'P2: channel1.dat is channel 1 ...'}. The sources, taps, throttle and xlating filters all use samp_rate, so the change produces a 48 kHz input and a 6 kHz output.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel breaks as P_INPUT (P1), or as 'P1, P2', in build.py MUTATIONS, then regenerate.

findings.claim: The approved plan (Phase 3) says L2 tasks come 'from converted examples', with the deterministic composer reserved for L1 chains of at most 5 blocks. This item is a composed L2 graph, as the workflow slot brief requested. Contamination control then rests on compose.signature, which compose.py documents as an L1 linear-chain mechanism and which follows only the last edge out of a fan-out. That is why F2 matters.
findings.evidence: Plan file take-a-look-at-cozy-crescent.md Phase 3: 'Both L1 (from the deterministic composer of ≤ 5-block single-rate chains) and L2 (from converted examples).' compose.py docstring: 'Programmatic L1 chains ... ≤ 5 blocks, single-rate chain'. signature() uses succ = {c[0]: c[2]}, last edge wins. Composed L2 items also exist in test (gbf-test-13/14/18/20), so this is a set-level deviation, not specific to this author.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the composed-L2 decision (and a branch-aware signature) to the team on the review sheet. If composed L2 is kept, extend compose.signature to canonicalise branching graphs and drop inert blocks before splitting (see F2).

item-quality.verdict:
The item mostly holds up. The instruction is solvable and self-contained, and it states every number the oracle uses (40 kHz, 6.4 kHz at 0.8, 8.2 kHz at 0.5, centres 6 and 8.5 kHz, decimation 8 to 5 kHz, signed tones at +400 and -300 Hz with amplitudes 0.4 and 0.25, the 40 dB combined-residual rule, the file names and complex type). Each oracle check maps to a spec property, the build/L2 labels are right (8 functional blocks, decimation, filtering), and the canary appears only in task.json. The reference passes V6 in my environment.

I ran 21 alternative solutions through ./gb ladder (scratch: WSL ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-06/alt, alt2, alt3). Valid alternatives were never wrongly rejected: band-pass-then-decimate-then-rotate, rotator plus rational resampler with a sine-phase source, Frequency Xlating with fcf taps, Hann, Blackman-Harris and Kaiser-40/45 windows, full-path file names and a 1-second Head all pass. Wrong designs fail as they should: rectangular window, a transition width of 1500 Hz, and a Hilbert front end.

Two medium findings survive: an unstated minimum run length, and a Throttle added only to move the chain hash into dev when its throttle-free form hashes to train. Two low findings: the stated filter cutoff and transition width are effectively not checked, and the real-to-complex conversion method is only implied by the expected amplitude.

findings.claim: Hidden requirement: the flowgraph must deliver at least 4400 output samples per channel, which needs at least 35,200 input samples, but the instruction never says to keep it running or not to limit the number of samples. A correct DDC bounded by a Head block fails V5 even though its signals are right.
findings.evidence: I added a Head (float, num_items 20000) after the Throttle in otherwise unchanged reference.grc (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-06/alt3/g_head_20000.grc). Result: highest=V4, V5 error "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'ch1': 2500, 'ch2': 2500}". With num_items=samp_rate it passes V6. A natural power-of-two choice of 32768 input samples gives 32768/8 = 4096 < 4400 and would also fail. Sibling items include the sentence "The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples." (gbf-dev-01, -02, -03, -07; gbf-test-01, -02, -04, -07); gbf-dev-06 does not. A related run-time risk: a Throttle set to samp_rate/decim on the input still passes, but takes 8.1 s of the 10 s timeout_s (alt/c_slow_throttle.grc).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the standard sentence to the instruction, for example: "The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples." Optionally raise timeout_s, or note in the contract that roughly 0.9 s of output is read.

findings.claim: The Throttle was added to the reference only to move the chain signature into dev (build.py says so). The task's natural form, which every variant and any typical model answer takes, has a signature that hashes to train. So the signature partition gives this item no protection against a template twin on the training side, and task.json does not flag this for the team.
findings.evidence: compose.signature_split results: with Throttle 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|blocks_throttle2|freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx|blocks_file_sink' -> dev. Without Throttle 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx|blocks_file_sink' -> train. With the old 'blocks_throttle' id -> train. With '...|blocks_float_to_complex|freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx|...' -> train. build.py docstring: "The Throttle is part of the reference only ...; it puts the chain signature in the dev partition (compose.signature_split). The instruction does not ask for it." The compose.py docstring says the partition exists so that a held-out chain "is never a template twin of a training chain", and training generators may build any chain whose signature hashes to train. Plan Phase 3 assigns signature partitioning to L1 composer chains; this is a branching composed L2 graph where signature() follows only one path. gbf-test-01 records the same twin risk in its authoring_notes ('team_decisions'); gbf-dev-06 has empty review notes and no authoring notes.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the twin risk for the team: add authoring_notes or review notes saying the throttle-free twin hashes to train, and ask that training-side composed-chain generation exclude two-channel DDC / frequency-translating channelizer themes. Alternatively, choose a reference whose natural, throttle-free form hashes to dev, or cluster on a theme rather than on the raw signature.

findings.claim: The instruction requires "a cutoff of 1 kHz, a transition width of 500 Hz" and channels "2 kHz wide", but no spec property covers these and the two-tone input cannot observe them. Clearly different filters pass V6, so the wording is stricter than the oracle.
findings.evidence: Reference with chan_taps changed passes all six V6 checks with: cutoff 650 Hz (rms ch1 0.3838), cutoff 1500 Hz, cutoff 1700 Hz (band_fraction ch2 0.99999), and cutoff 1000 Hz with transition 100 Hz (alt/a_cutoff650, a_cutoff1500, a_cutoff1700, a_tw100). Only transition 1500 Hz fails (ch1 rms 0.369). spec_properties P1-P5 do not mention cutoff or transition width.
findings.suggested_fix: Document this as unchecked wording in authoring notes, as gbf-test-01 does, so the team knows the filter shape is only checked through selectivity and gain at the two carrier offsets. Alternatively, add a probe tone in each channel's stopband just past 1.25 kHz offset, or near the passband edge, to bound the cutoff. Another option is to word the filter numbers as design guidance and keep the 40 dB selectivity as the requirement.

findings.claim: The instruction says how to process each channel (shift to 0 Hz to get complex baseband, low-pass with passband gain 1, decimate by 8) but not how to turn the real input into complex samples. A Hilbert/analytic-signal front end satisfies every procedural sentence yet fails rms at twice the stated amplitude. Only the 'Expected result' amplitude, with its half-amplitude explanation, rules it out.
findings.evidence: alt/d_hilbert.grc (hilbert_fc with 129 taps, then freq_xlating ccc with firdes.low_pass(1, 40000, 1000, 500), decimation 8) gives peak_freq +400 / -300 and band_fraction 1.0 (pass), but rms 0.7999 / 0.4987 against 0.4 / 0.25 (fail). The oracle agrees with the stated expected amplitude, so this is not a wrong rejection. The cost is that a careful expert must reconcile the procedure with the stated outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: add a clause such as "treat the real samples as complex samples with a zero imaginary part", or state that the expected amplitudes apply to the whole chain, so that the gain-1 filter and the half-amplitude result cannot be read as conflicting.
